turns.reply:
`sync_avatars.py` now treats a 404 as "this user has no avatar": it skips that user, carries on with the rest, and exits 0 with nothing on stderr, so cron stays quiet.

I checked it against a local test server, not your real CDN:

- **One user returning 404:** the other avatars were written, exit code 0, stderr empty, and stdout read `synced 2 avatars, 1 users have no avatar`.
- **One user returning 500:** the script still dies with the traceback on stderr and exit code 1, so you still get the email.

Only 404 is silenced. Timeouts, 5xx responses and connection failures still fail loudly, so a real CDN outage will still email the team.

Previously the script stopped at the first 404, so every user after it in `users.json` was not synced on those nights. That is fixed as a side effect.

Decision for you: when a user deletes their avatar, the previously mirrored `avatars/<id>.png` is left in place, so the mirror keeps serving the old picture. I did not delete it because that local file may be the last copy. Removing it on 404 is a one-line change if you want the mirror to follow deletions — say if you want it.
